summary: Planned the implementation of the `conan lock remove` command and dynamic tracking syntax for `<host_version:pkg_name>`.
content:
## Analysis & Plan

The deliverable is broken down into two main domains:

1.  **Lockfile Require Removal:** The new `conan lock remove` command requires updates to both the CLI layer and the `Lockfile` internal data structures. Due to the reliance on `OrderedDict` for lockfile requirements, deleting items directly during iteration throws a runtime error. This necessitates a safe, two-pass deletion mechanism. We will add `remove` primitives to the `Lockfile` and `_LockRequires` models, followed by the CLI subcommand and `LockfileAPI` hooks.
2.  **Dynamic Version Tracking:** The graph builder logic needs to parse the new `<host_version:pkg_name>` syntax. Instead of blindly updating the version field on an existing `RecipeReference` in-place, we must construct a new `RecipeReference` using the transitive dependency's specific state (version, user, channel) and permanently assign it to `require.ref`. This ensures that downstream lockfile serializers correctly persist the concrete resolved state rather than the literal `"<host_version>"` token.

findings.description: Modifying lockfile requirement dictionaries during iteration causes runtime failures; two-pass deletion is mandatory.
To correctly capture concrete versions in lockfiles, the `Requirement.ref` must be completely reassigned rather than mutating the version string on the original reference object in-place.

children.title: Implement safe two-pass requirement removal in `Lockfile` state
children.description: Add logic to safely remove requirements from the internal lockfile state structures.
acceptance_criteria: `_LockRequires.remove(ref)` identifies matching references using a two-pass strategy (collect first, then delete).
Matches are determined by evaluating `k.name == ref.name` and optionally `k.version == ref.version` if the version is provided.
Dictionary mutation exceptions are entirely avoided during removal.

children.title: Implement `conan lock remove` subcommand (CLI & API)
children.description: Expose the lockfile requirement removal functionality via the CLI.
acceptance_criteria: The CLI parses `--requires`, `--build-requires`, and `--python-requires` as `RecipeReference` objects.
The command leverages `conan_api.lockfile.remove_lockfile()` which safely calls `Lockfile.remove()`.
The updated lockfile is cleanly serialized to disk without the target requirements.

children.title: Implement `<host_version:pkg_name>` dynamic tracking & state propagation
children.description: Parse the tracking syntax and permanently update the `Requirement.ref` state.
acceptance_criteria: The `pkg_name` target is extracted and used to query `node.transitive_deps`.
`require.ref` is fully re-assigned to a new `RecipeReference` holding the concrete version, user, and channel from the target dependency.
Missing target dependencies throw explicit `ConanException` strings.
The concrete version state cleanly persists to generated lockfiles, completely removing the original `<host_version:pkg_name>` syntax token from tracked references.

children.title: Functional testing for lock remove and dynamic tracking
children.description: Add robust integration tests verifying both the lock remove and dynamic tracking capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert that `conan lock remove` completely purges designated elements without errors.
Tests assert the `<host_version:pkg_name>` tracking syntax extracts the targeted transitive dependency correctly.
Lockfiles generated during these tests correctly display the final resolved versions.
